class.name: FmodGeneralSettings
class.brief_description: The general FMOD settings, read from Project Settings.
class.description: Set in Project Settings under [code]Fmod/General[/code] and [code]Fmod/Output[/code]. FMOD reads them when it initializes.

members.member: The folder holding the project's banks. The editor's bank explorer reads the banks from it, and exports pack them.
The maximum number of channels FMOD plays at once.
The number of listeners FMOD starts with.
The Godot audio bus FMOD's sound plays on, with [constant GODOT_BUS] output.
When FMOD mixes its sound for the Godot bus.
If [code]true[/code], FMOD Studio can connect to the running game to edit and profile its audio live. Never enabled in the editor.
If [code]true[/code], FMOD tracks its memory use, reported to FMOD Studio's profiler.
If [code]true[/code], event emitters find their event by path rather than by GUID.
Where FMOD Studio carries out what your game asks it: starting and stopping events, setting parameters, moving sounds.
If [code]true[/code], FMOD mixes at Godot's mix rate ([code]audio/driver/mix_rate[/code]) instead of the sample rate of [FmodSoftwareFormatSettings], so Godot does not convert FMOD's sound.

constants.constant: On FMOD's own thread: costs your frames nothing, but a request can wait up to 20 ms.
In [method FmodServer.update], on the main thread: requests apply right away, at the cost of frame time.
Straight to the audio device, as FMOD always did.
Onto a Godot audio bus: its effects and volume, Mute Game and Movie Maker then apply to FMOD. Not on the web.
Ahead of time: protects against crackles, adds about 40 ms of delay.
When Godot asks: shortest delay, and the one for Movie Maker. A very heavy FMOD scene can crackle.
